title: Burmese fried rice (htamin gyaw)
steps: Scramble the eggs in a little oil in a hot wok and set aside.
Fry the garlic and onion, then add the chicken and cook through.
Add the rice and break up the lumps, stir-frying for 3 minutes.
Add the peas, soy sauce, fish sauce and pepper and toss.
Return the eggs and mix gently, then serve topped with fried onions.

title: Burmese fritters (a-kyaw, vegetable fritters in chickpea batter)

ingredients.name: gourd or pumpkin, cut into thin strips

steps: Whisk the flours, turmeric, salt and water into a thick batter.
Fold in the onion, gourd and bean sprouts.
Heat the oil to about 180°C.
Drop spoonfuls of batter into the oil and fry for 3 to 4 minutes until crisp and golden.
Drain on paper and serve hot with tamarind chili sauce.

title: Burmese milk tea (laphet yay)
steps: Boil the water with the tea and salt and simmer for 15 minutes until very dark.
Strain the tea into a pot or jug.
Put condensed milk and evaporated milk into the cups, adjusting amounts to taste.
Pour in the hot tea.
Pour the tea back and forth between two cups or jugs from a height to cool and froth it, then serve.

title: Burmese tofu (chickpea tofu)
steps: Whisk the chickpea flour with 300 ml of cold water until smooth.
Bring the remaining water to a boil with the turmeric and salt.
Pour the batter into the boiling water slowly, whisking constantly.
Cook on low for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring, until the mixture is thick and glossy.
Pour into an oiled tray and let it set and cool for an hour.
Cut into cubes and dress with oil, lime, soy sauce, garlic and coriander.

title: Burmese tofu fritters (to hpu gyaw)

ingredients.name: set Burmese chickpea tofu (about 200 g flour cooked as above), cooled and cut into pieces

steps: Cut the set tofu into thick fingers or triangles and pat dry.
Heat the oil to 180°C.
Fry the tofu in batches for 4 to 5 minutes until crisp outside and soft inside.
Drain well on paper.
Mix the tamarind, sugar, chili flakes, water and salt for a dipping sauce.
Serve hot with the sauce.

title: Hsi htamin (Burmese turmeric sticky rice)
steps: Drain the soaked rice and mix with turmeric, salt and a spoonful of oil.
Steam the rice over boiling water for 30 to 35 minutes until tender and sticky.
Heat the rest of the oil in a pan and fry the onion until golden.
Turn the hot rice out and fluff gently, folding in half of the fried onion.
Serve topped with sesame seeds, the remaining onion and peas on the side.

title: Kat kyi kaik (Burmese stir-fried flat noodles with seafood)
steps: Soak the noodles in warm water until pliable and drain.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the garlic for 10 seconds.
Add the squid and prawns and stir-fry 2 minutes until just done.
Add the noodles and both soy sauces, tossing quickly. Use kitchen scissors to cut the noodles into shorter pieces as they cook.
Add the peas, bean sprouts and spring onions and toss for another minute.
Season with pepper and serve right away.

title: Khanon htok (Burmese rolled omelette snack with chicken)
steps: Fry the onion and garlic in a tablespoon of oil, add the chicken and shrimp and cook through, then season with fish sauce and pepper.
Whisk the eggs, flour and water into a thin batter.
Pour a thin layer into an oiled non-stick pan and swirl to make a wide crepe-like omelette.
Spoon filling along one side and roll up, then tuck in the ends.
Cook until golden, and slice into pieces to serve.

title: Khauk swè thoke (Burmese wheat noodle salad)

ingredients.name: chickpea flour, toasted in a dry pan

steps: Cook the noodles in boiling water until tender, rinse in cold water and drain well.
Mix the toasted chickpea flour with the lime juice, soy sauce, chili flakes, ground dried shrimp and some fried-onion oil to make a thick dressing.
Toss the noodles with the dressing until each strand is coated.
Add the shredded chicken, cabbage and carrot and mix again.
Top with fried onions, fried garlic and coriander, adding more lime or chili to taste, and serve at room temperature.

source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Kya zan hinga (Burmese glass noodle soup)

ingredients.name: dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and sliced

steps: Heat the stock with the garlic, mushrooms and lily buds and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the bean curd skin, shrimp and fish sauce and cook for 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the soaked glass noodles and heat through.
Season with pepper and more fish sauce to taste.
Serve garnished with coriander, shallots and a squeeze of lime.

title: Kyay oh (Burmese pork and vermicelli noodle soup)

ingredients.name: minced pork, shaped into small balls

steps: Fry the garlic in the oil until golden, then add the sliced pork and stir for 3 minutes.
Add the stock, fish sauce and pepper and simmer for 20 minutes.
Drop in the pork balls, then the liver, and cook for 5 minutes more.
Beat the eggs and drizzle into the simmering soup so they form threads.
Soak the vermicelli in hot water until soft and blanch the greens.
Put noodles and greens in bowls, ladle the soup over and top with fried garlic, coriander and chili.

title: Lahpet thoke (Burmese pickled tea leaf salad)

ingredients.name: lahpet (Burmese pickled tea leaves, from a jar)
fried broad beans or yellow split peas

steps: Squeeze the lahpet lightly and mix with the lime juice and oil to loosen it.
Place the cabbage and tomato in the middle of a plate or bowl.
Arrange the peanuts, fried beans, sesame seeds, fried garlic and dried shrimp in separate small piles around it, with the dressed tea leaves in a mound.
Scatter over the sliced chili and add fish sauce to taste.
At the table, toss everything together so every bite carries crunch, sour tea and fresh vegetables.

title: Mont lone yay baw (Burmese water-ball rice dumplings with jaggery)
steps: Mix both flours with the salt and enough warm water to make a smooth dough that does not crack.
Roll the dough into balls about 2.5 cm wide.
Flatten each ball, press a piece of jaggery into the centre and seal it completely.
Boil the dumplings in plenty of water until they all float, 3 to 5 minutes.
Lift them out and drain, then roll in coconut mixed with a pinch of salt.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Nan gyi thoke (Burmese thick rice noodle salad with chicken)
steps: Simmer the chicken with a pinch of salt until cooked, then shred it, reserving a little broth.
Toast the chickpea flour in a dry pan until pale golden and fragrant, then stir in a little hot broth to make a smooth, thick paste.
Heat the oil and fry the garlic and onion with the turmeric until soft, add the chicken and the fish sauce and cook 3 minutes.
Cook the noodles until tender and drain.
Toss the noodles with the chicken mixture and chickpea paste.
Serve topped with egg, coriander and chili oil, with lime wedges on the side.

title: Ngapyaw baung (Burmese banana pudding in coconut milk)
steps: Pour the coconut milk and milk into a pan and add the sugar and salt.
Heat gently until the sugar dissolves.
Add the bananas and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, without stirring too much so they keep their shape, until soft.
Spoon into bowls and sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds.
Serve warm or chilled.

title: Ohn no khao swè (Burmese coconut chicken noodle soup)

ingredients.name: chickpea flour, mixed with 100 ml water

ingredients.measure: fried onions, coriander, chili flakes, lime
ingredients.name: to serve

steps: Fry the onion in the oil until soft and golden, add the garlic, ginger, turmeric and paprika and stir for a minute.
Add the chicken and cook until lightly browned.
Pour in the stock, coconut milk and fish sauce and simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in the chickpea flour mixture and simmer until the soup thickens to a creamy consistency.
Cook the noodles separately and drain.
Place noodles in bowls, ladle the soup over and serve with eggs, fried onions, coriander, chili flakes and lime.

title: Pathein halawa (Burmese sticky rice flour sweet)
steps: Mix both flours with the coconut milk and milk into a smooth batter, then add the sugar.
Melt the butter in a heavy pan and add the batter.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens into a sticky mass that pulls away from the pan.
Stir in the coconut and cook 5 minutes more.
Turn into a greased tray, scatter with poppy seeds and let it set.
Cut into squares when cool.

title: Pe htaw bhut htamin (Burmese buttered lentil rice)

ingredients.name: split yellow lentils or dried chickpeas, soaked

steps: Wash the rice and drain.
Melt the butter in a pot, add the spices and the soaked lentils and fry for a minute.
Add the rice and fry until glossy and coated.
Pour in the water, add salt and bring to a boil.
Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes, then rest for 10 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and scatter with cashews, raisins and fried onions.

title: Sanwin makin (Burmese semolina cake)
steps: Heat the coconut milk, water, sugar and butter until the sugar dissolves.
Stir in the semolina and cook, stirring constantly, until it thickens to a heavy porridge.
Cool for 10 minutes, then beat in the eggs one at a time and fold in the raisins and cashews.
Pour into a greased baking dish and sprinkle with poppy seeds.
Bake at 180°C for 35 to 40 minutes until set and golden on top.
Cool before cutting into diamonds.

title: Shan meeshay (Burmese Shan rice noodles with pork sauce)
steps: Heat the oil and fry the garlic, then add the pork and brown it.
Stir in the tomatoes, soy sauce, soybean paste and chili flakes and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the water and simmer for 10 minutes more until thick and saucy.
Boil the noodles until soft and drain.
Divide into bowls, top with the sauce and pickled mustard greens, and sprinkle with fried garlic and coriander.

title: Shwe yin aye (Burmese cool coconut milk dessert)
steps: Warm the coconut milk, water, sugar and salt in a pan until the sugar dissolves, then chill thoroughly.
Prepare the sago, jelly and rice and let them cool.
Place spoonfuls of each in tall glasses with the bread cubes.
Pour the chilled coconut milk over.
Add ice and serve cold.

title: Talabaw (Karen bamboo shoot soup)

ingredients.name: bamboo shoots (canned, rinsed, or fresh and boiled)
firm white fish fillet or pork

steps: Boil the bamboo shoots in water for 10 minutes and drain, to remove any bitterness.
Bring the water to a boil with the lemongrass and onion, then add the bamboo shoots and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the fish or pork and cook until done.
Stir in the ground rice and simmer until the soup thickens slightly.
Season with fish sauce and pepper.
Finish with basil and chili, and serve with a little steamed rice.
